title: The Discovery of Oz, the Terrible, part 8
attribution: From The Wonderful Wizard of Oz by L. Frank Baum (1900), via Project Gutenberg, in reading order.
body: “Very well,” answered Oz meekly. “Come to me tomorrow and you shall have a heart. I have played Wizard for so many years that I may as well continue the part a little longer.”
“And now,” said Dorothy, “how am I to get back to Kansas?”

“We shall have to think about that,” replied the little man. “Give me two or three days to consider the matter and I’ll try to find a way to carry you over the desert. In the meantime you shall all be treated as my guests, and while you live in the Palace my people will wait upon you and obey your slightest wish. There is only one thing I ask in return for my help—such as it is. You must keep my secret and tell no one I am a humbug.”

They agreed to say nothing of what they had learned, and went back to their rooms in high spirits. Even Dorothy had hope that “The Great and Terrible Humbug,” as she called him, would find a way to send her back to Kansas, and if he did she was willing to forgive him everything.

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does Oz ask in return for his help?
options: That they keep his secret and tell no one
That they give back the Golden Cap
That they stay in the Palace for a year
That they never speak to him again

questions.prompt: Per the passage, how long does Oz ask for to think about Kansas?
options: Two or three days
A single night
A whole month
Until the spring

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does Oz say about carrying Dorothy?
options: He will try to find a way over the desert
He will send the Winged Monkeys with her
He cannot possibly help her at all
He will go with her as far as Omaha

questions.prompt: Per the passage, how will they live in the meantime?
options: As his guests, waited on by his people
As servants in the Palace kitchens
In an inn in the city streets
Camped outside the green wall

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what name does Dorothy give him?
options: The Great and Terrible Humbug
The Little Old Man of Omaha
The Wizard of the Green Glasses
The Very Bad Wizard

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why does Oz agree to give the Woodman a heart?
options: He may as well play the Wizard a little longer
He has found a real heart in his cupboard
The Woodman threatened him with his axe
Dorothy insisted that he keep his promise

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, how did the four feel as they went back to their rooms?
options: In high spirits
Bitterly disappointed
Angry with the Wizard
Frightened of being overheard

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, on what condition would Dorothy forgive him everything?
options: If he found a way to send her back to Kansas
If he told his people the truth about himself
If he gave her friends their gifts first
If he came with them across the desert

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does meekly describe about Oz's answer?
options: Given quietly, without any resistance
Given proudly, as a great favour
Given angrily, after an argument
Given slowly, after long thought

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the passage?
options: A bargain of secrecy for gifts, and hope restored on both sides
A refusal that leaves the travellers with nothing
A quarrel in which the Wizard is exposed to his people
A decision to leave the Emerald City that same night

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what did they agree to do?
options: Say nothing of what they had learned
Leave the city within three days
Give the Wizard back the Golden Cap
Tell the people the whole truth

questions.prompt: Per the passage, what will the Wizard's people do for them?
options: Wait upon them and obey their slightest wish
Guard them until the Wizard decides
Show them the road across the desert
Make them each a suit of green clothes

questions.prompt: According to the passage, when is the Woodman to come for his heart?
options: Tomorrow
That same evening
In two or three days
After Dorothy leaves

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what is the desert the obstacle to?
options: Getting Dorothy back to Kansas
Reaching the Winkie country
Finding the Witch of the South
Sending the Monkeys home

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what does Dorothy's nickname for Oz suggest?
options: She now sees the grand title and the fraud together
She still believes he is a great and terrible wizard
She has decided never to speak to him again
She thinks he is more dangerous than the Witches

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does in high spirits mean?
options: Cheerful and hopeful again
Angry and ready to argue
Tired out but relieved
Frightened of what comes next

questions.prompt: Which of these best summarises the passage?
options: A secret kept in exchange for gifts, and hope for the journey home
A wizard who admits he can do nothing for any of them
A plan to cross the desert agreed on that same day
A quarrel about whether to tell the people the truth
